evidence.evidence_text: Nestled on the eastern shore of Hoan Kiem Lake in Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, the "Ready to Die for the Fatherland to Live" Monument stands as a silent sentinel, a testament to the indomitable spirit of Hanoi's defenders during a pivotal moment in Vietnam's history. Erected to honor the brave soldiers of the Capital Regiment and the resilient citizens of Hanoi who fought valiantly for 60 days and nights at the close of 1946, this monument commemorates the onset of the resistance war against French colonial rule.
